items.title: 13.6 Bond ki taqat ke lihaz se hydrogen halides ki nisbati thermal stability (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 13.6 with Table 13.5 and Quick Check 13.3, printed pages 296-297.

blocks.text: Halogen group mein fluorine se iodine tak neeche jate hue hydrogen halides (H–X) ki thermal stability (garmi mein na tootne ki salahiyat) kam hoti jati hai, kyun ke Table 13.5 ke mutabiq bond dissociation energy (bond todne ke liye zaroori energy) kam hoti hai. HX ki thermal stability ki tarteeb yeh hai:

Is trend ki wajah H–X molecule mein hydrogen aur halogen atom ke darmiyan bond ki taqat hai. Hydrogen fluoride (HF) sab se zyada thermally stable hydrogen halide hai. Fluorine ki zyada electronegativity aur chhote atomic radius ki wajah se orbitals ka overlap (aapas mein milna) mazboot hota hai aur H–F bond bohat mazboot banta hai. H–F ki bond dissociation energy (569 kJ/mol) tamam hydrogen halides mein sab se zyada hai. Hydrogen chloride (HCl) HF se kam magar baqi hydrogen halides se zyada stable hai. Chlorine ka atomic radius fluorine se bara hai, is liye H–Cl bond H–F se kamzor hai; is ki bond dissociation energy 431 kJ/mol hai. Bromine ka radius aur bara hai, is liye orbitals ka overlap kam hota hai aur H–Br bond H–F aur H–Cl dono se kamzor hai; is ki bond dissociation energy 366 kJ/mol hai. Aam hydrogen halides mein hydrogen iodide (HI) sab se kam thermally stable hai. Iodine ka atomic radius bohat bara hai, overlap kamzor hota hai, is liye H–I bond sab se kamzor hai; is ki bond dissociation energy 299 kJ/mol hai.

blocks.prompt: a) Halogens ki oxidizing power aur un ke standard reduction potential ka kya taalluq hai?
blocks.explanation: E° jitna zyada positive, halogen utni aasani se electron leta hai aur utna taqatwar oxidizing agent hai. F₂ (+2.87 V) sab se taqatwar aur I₂ (+0.54 V) sab se kamzor hai.

blocks.prompt: b) H₂ aur F₂ ka reaction dhamake wala hai magar H₂ aur I₂ ka aahista aur reversible. Kyun?
blocks.explanation: Banne wala H–F bond (569 kJ mol⁻¹) toote wale F–F bond (156 kJ mol⁻¹) se bohat mazboot hai, is liye bohat energy nikalti hai aur reaction dhamake se hota hai. H–I bond (299 kJ mol⁻¹) kamzor hai, thori energy nikalti hai, reaction ko garmi aur catalyst chahiye, aur kamzor HI wapas toot jata hai, is liye reaction reversible hai.

blocks.prompt: c) Table 13.4 aur 13.5 se batayein: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl aur H₂ + Br₂ → 2HBr mein kaun zyada exothermic hai?
blocks.explanation: H₂ + Cl₂ zyada exothermic hai. Is mein 431 kJ mol⁻¹ wale do H–Cl bond bante hain jab ke H₂ + Br₂ mein sirf 366 kJ mol⁻¹ wale do H–Br bond bante hain. Cl–Cl (243) todne mein Br–Br (193) se kuch zyada energy lagti hai, phir bhi naye bonds se nikalne wali energy ka farq bohat bara hai. Cl₂ ka E° (+1.36 V) bhi Br₂ (+1.07 V) se zyada hai, yani chlorine zyada taqatwar oxidizing agent hai.

blocks.prompt: d) Hydrogen halides ki thermal stability bond dissociation energy se kaise judi hai?
blocks.explanation: H–X bond jitna mazboot (bond dissociation energy jitni zyada), use todne ke liye utni zyada garmi chahiye, is liye molecule utna zyada thermally stable hai: HF (569) > HCl (431) > HBr (366) > HI (299 kJ mol⁻¹).

blocks.prompt: e) HF sab se zyada thermally stable hydrogen halide kyun hai?
blocks.explanation: Fluorine chhota aur sab se zyada electronegative hai, is liye hydrogen ke saath is ke orbitals ka overlap bohat mazboot hota hai. H–F bond sab se mazboot (569 kJ mol⁻¹) hai, is liye HF garmi se sab se mushkil se toot-ta hai.

items: Thermal stability: HF > HCl > HBr > HI.
Bond dissociation energy 569, 431, 366, 299 kJ mol⁻¹: bara atom, kam overlap, kamzor bond, kam stability.
